en: The Section of Threes, Chapter on the Well (Udapānavagga)
1. The Jātaka of the Polluter of the Well “Of the forest-dwelling seer,
who has practiced austerities for a long time...”
“How did you drain this well that was so laboriously made?
“This is the nature of jackals,” he replied.
"Having drunk that by which we are refreshed—
the Dhamma of our father and grandfather—
you ought not to find fault with it."
“For those of you whose Dhamma is such as this,
what then is non-Dhamma? Do not [confuse] Dhamma with non-Dhamma.”
"We have never seen [such a thing] at any time.
This concludes the first Jātaka, the Udapānadūsaka-jātaka.
